intro: Lesson 17: The Domesday Book. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A great survey
points: Who owned what, and what it was worth

model.title: An entry: a village has 10 households, 2 ploughs, a mill, 40 pigs

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A small farming village with woodland and a mill

keywords.def: William's great survey of England in 1086
money people must pay to the ruler
something that tells us about the past

questions.q: Why did William want to know how many ploughs there were?
questions.a: To work out how valuable the land was and what tax it could pay

questions.q: Where is the Domesday Book kept today?
Is the Domesday Book a primary or secondary source?
questions.a: Primary: it was made at the time

questions.q: Core: Read three example entries and write what each tells us about the place.
Extend: What does the Domesday Book NOT tell us?
questions.a: For example: what people thought or felt, women's names, daily life

questions.q: Stretch: Write a Domesday-style entry for your street (houses, cars, shops, trees).
questions.a: An entry in the same style

questions.q: The Domesday Book was written in:
questions.a: B) 1086. William ordered it in 1085 and it was written in 1086.

questions.q: Big question: why count every pig?
questions.a: To know the wealth of the land, so William could tax it and control it
